'''Rayford Trae Young''' (born September 19, 1998) is an American basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]]. In January 2017, Young was selected as a [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.maxpreps.com/news/-c4H_udHpk68Wy2LGvrS3Q/2017-mcdonald’s-all-american-game-boys-rosters-announced.htm | title = 2017 McDonald’s All-American Game boys rosters announced | work = maxpreps | date = 15 January 2017 | accessdate = 20 February 2017}}</ref> On December 19, 2017, with 22 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] he tied the [[NCAA]] single-game record, shared by Syracuse's [[Sherman Douglas]] (1989), Southern's [[Avery Johnson]] (1988) and Charleston Southern's [[Tony Fairley]] (1987).<ref>{{cite news |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |title=Trae Young first in two decades to have 20-point, 20-assist game |date=December 20, 2017 |work=ESPN |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21821872/trae-young-oklahoma-ties-ncaa-record-22-assists-win-northwestern-state }}</ref> By the end of his only college season, Young would be the first and only player to ever lead the NCAA in both points and assists in a single season.

==Early life==
Born in [[Lubbock, Texas]], Trae is the son of Candice and Rayford Young.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trae Young Bio|url=http://www.soonersports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211670156|website=OU Athletics|language=en}}</ref> He has a younger brother, Timothy, and two younger sisters, Caitlyn and Camryn. Trae's father played basketball at [[Texas Tech University|Texas Tech]] and professionally in Europe.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/y/young-trae.aspx|title=Trae Young|website=Usab.com|accessdate=13 December 2017}}</ref>

==High school career==
Young attended [[Norman North High School]] in his hometown of [[Norman, Oklahoma|Norman]], [[Oklahoma]]. While Young did not play basketball in his freshman year at Norman North, he ended up playing for the team in his sophomore year. That year, he averaged 25 points, 5 assists, and 4 rebounds per game as he helped Norman North win the 2015 area championship and was named Oklahoma's Sophomore of the Year. During his junior year of high school, he significantly improved his game, averaging 34.2 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 4.6 assists as he led the team to a 28–4 record that year, winning the regional title and placing runner up in the 2016 Oklahoma Class 6A championship game. He was also named Oklahoma's Player of the Year by multiple sources. In his senior season, he averaged 42.6 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game while also shooting at a 48.9% rate.

===Recruiting===
Young was considered one of the best players in the 2017 recruiting class by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Trae-Young-56638|title=Trae Young, Oklahoma Sooners, Point Guard|website=247Sports|accessdate=13 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/203210/trae-young|title=Trae Young - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=13 December 2017}}</ref> ESPN considered him the second-best point guard prospect that year, while the other websites considered him the third-best point guard of the recruiting class that year. On February 16, 2017, Young committed to the Oklahoma Sooners, having him stay in his home state for his college career. He was the [[University of Oklahoma]]'s first five-star recruit since [[Tiny Gallon]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/08/23/oklahoma-sooners-roster-freshmen-trae-young|title=Trae Young plays pivotal role for rebuilding Sooners|website=Si.com|accessdate=13 December 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
On February 16, 2017, Trae Young committed to the Oklahoma Sooners. At the start of the season, on November 12, Young recorded 15 points, 10 assists, and 6 rebounds in a win over [[Omaha University]]. Three days after his college debut, Young recorded 22 points and a then season-high 13 assists in a win over [[Ball State University]]. On November 26, Young recorded a season-high 43 points and 7 assists in a 90–80 win over the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. That game had his name draw multiple comparisons to [[Stephen Curry]] in terms of his playing style.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2017/11/28/16707480/oklahoma-trae-young-stats-stephen-curry-comparison-sooners-basketball|title=Oklahoma's Trae Young is becoming college basketball’s next Stephen Curry|website=Sbnation.com|accessdate=13 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/12/18/nba-draft-trae-young-oklahoma-nba-comparison-stephen-curry|title=NBA Draft Dispatch: Finding Trae Young's NBA comp|date=December 18, 2017|website=SI.com|access-date=January 11, 2018}}</ref> On December 19, Young tied ([[Sherman Douglas]], [[Tony Fairley]], and [[Avery Johnson]]) the NCAA single-game assists record with 22, while also recording 26 points in a blowout 105–68 win against the [[Northwestern State Demons basketball|Northwestern State Demons]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/oklahoma-freshman-phenom-trae-young-ties-ncaa-record-with-22-assists/|title=Oklahoma freshman phenom Trae Young ties NCAA record with 22 assists|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=December 20, 2017|language=en}}</ref> Throughout the season, Young rose from being a late first-round or a second-round pick to being a potential top-three pick for the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/12/04/nba-mock-draft-2018-deandre-ayton-luka-doncic-marvin-bagley|title=NBA Mock Draft 2.0: Will big men own the lottery?|date=December 4, 2017|website=SI.com|access-date=January 11, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://uproxx.com/dimemag/nba-mock-draft-preseason-chicago-bulls-2018-marvin-bagley-luke-doncic/|title=NBA Mock Draft 2018: The Chicago Bulls And Everyone Else|date=October 17, 2017|website=Uproxx.com|access-date=January 11, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/news/nba-mock-draft-2018-picks-order-celtics-bulls-cavs-trae-young-luka-doncic-marvin-bagley-iii/119ce0w8ia7t315l8og30rnsm1|title=NBA Mock Draft 2018: Oklahoma's Trae Young flies into top five on latest board|date=January 8, 2018|website=SportingNews.com|access-date=January 11, 2018}}</ref> He also garnered praise from both [[LeBron James]] and [[Stephen Curry]] for his season with Oklahoma.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2018/01/05/trae-young-nba-draft-prospect-debate-oklahoma-stephen-curry|title=The most entertaining NBA draft debate in years|date=January 5, 2018|website=SI.com|access-date=January 11, 2018}}</ref> Young, however, ran into a rough patch when [[West Virginia University]]'s Press Virginia defense forced him into 8 turnovers on January 5, 2018. Furthermore, his individual defense has been rated as "poor".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/analysis/248567/Prospect-Report-Trae-Young-Of-Oklahoma|title=Prospect Report: Trae Young Of Oklahoma|first=Rafael|last=Uehara|date=January 10, 2018|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 11, 2018}}</ref> However, Young would recover with a season-high 43 points and 11 rebounds with 7 assists in a 102–97 overtime win over [[Texas Christian University]] a week later on January 13. Three days later, Young would wind up with a season-high 12 turnovers in a blowout loss to [[Kansas State University]], which surpassed his previous season-high a few weeks ago. On January 20, Young recorded a new career-high 48 points (albeit on 14/39 overall shooting) in a close 83–81 overtime loss to rivaling [[Oklahoma State University]]. He recovered from that with a 9 assist, 26 point effort (on 7/9 shooting) in an 85-80 win over #5-ranked [[University of Kansas]] on January 23rd.

Young finished his freshman regular season leading the country in many statistics: assists (271), turnovers (161), points (848), points per game (27.4), assists per game (8.7), and assist percentage (48.6%). The 811 points scored in the Big 12 would break the conference's record for most points scored by a freshman player, which was previously held by [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Michael Beasley]]. On March 7, 2018, Young was announced as the winner of the [[Wayman Tisdale Award]] for National Freshman of the Year by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] (USBWA).<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2018/tisdale180307.html |title=Oklahoma's Young wins Wayman Tisdale Award |publisher=USBWA |date=March 7, 2018 |accessdate=March 7, 2018}}</ref> At the end of the regular season for Oklahoma, Young was also named the Big 12's Freshman of the Year and was a member of the All-Big 12's First Team. In addition, he was also brought up as a consensus member of the All-American First Team, which was named throughout multiple organizations. Young also joined [[DeAndre Ayton]] and [[Marvin Bagley III]] as the first consensus All-American First-Team to have three freshman players be named there. On March 15, Young recorded 28 points, 7 assists, and 5 rebounds in a 83–78 overtime loss to No. 7 seed [[Rhode Island University]]. He became the second freshman to record similar numbers of points in an NCAA Tournament game, with [[Chris Paul]] being the first player back in 2004.<ref>http://www.oudaily.com/sports/oklahoma-basketball-trae-young-makes-history-as-freshman-in-ncaa/article_e2cc0362-2883-11e8-87eb-5b8ada24c230.html</ref> 

Following Oklahoma's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Young announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he is expected to be a first round selection.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22842249/oklahoma-sooners-freshman-guard-trae-young-enter-nba-draft|title=Oklahoma freshman guard Trae Young to enter NBA draft|access-date=2018-03-20|language=en-US}}</ref>

==National team career==
He was a member of the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|U.S. men's national U18 team]] that won a gold medal at the [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]].

==Player profile==
Young's game has been primarily influenced by [[Steve Nash]] and [[Stephen Curry]], to the point where he notes them as his favorite players at the game. His shooting ability has been compared positively to Stephen Curry's college years at [[Davidson College]] and his passing ability has been strongly influenced by [[Steve Nash]].
